records.region: Palo Blanco–Cedral–Matehuala–San Gabriel–El Milagro de Guadalupe interior plateau corridor, San Luis Potosí and adjacent Nuevo León
records.material_pending_reason: The chosen continuation from the San Gabriel convergence south through the interior plain toward El Milagro de Guadalupe and into the stored final turn west of San José del Refugio is not established as a continuous selected channel/through-link by the acquired sources. Basin membership, flood-prone terrain and local branch names do not replace this connection.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No natural river name is supported for the complete selected north-to-south route. The basin identity Matehuala is regional context and is not converted into a river name.
records.completion_scope: The northern valley and its joins through San Gabriel have bounded source correspondence. The selected continuation south toward El Milagro de Guadalupe and the actual terminal west of San José del Refugio remains incomplete.
records.supported_name_scope: Jaquis and La Milpita are labels on distinct western approaches; they are useful geographic distinctions, not selected-whole candidates. Locality names remain locality names.

scope_limits: No independently supported natural name was read for the selected trunk or terminal.
The acquired maps cover the selected regional extent, but the southern through-link remains substantive missing evidence; this is not a completed naming-scope hold.
Short local channel details and exact name-boundary/source/bank vertices are not demanded. No present flow, water level or reservoir-operation claim is made.
Source dates describe historical cartographic and field material, not a 2026 hydrologic observation.

records.region: Southern Mendoza and western Puelén, La Pampa: basaltic plateau west of Puelén
records.material_pending_reason: The chosen western opening, upper southward turn, long eastward plateau through-links and lower approach to the actual endpoint north of La Salinilla are not established as one connected drainage by the inspected sources.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No river or representative river-system name is supported for the complete selection. El Puesto and Pampa de Ranquelcó identify volcanic flows, while La Salinilla identifies a separate saline body south of the selected endpoint; none is assigned to the river.
records.completion_scope: The complete stored extent was considered against regional volcanic and saline-survey mapping. The actual opening, upper and middle drainage connections and final receiving endpoint remain unestablished; terrain coverage is not completed hydrographic correspondence.
records.supported_name_scope: No river or representative river-system name is supported for the complete selection. El Puesto and Pampa de Ranquelcó identify volcanic flows, while La Salinilla identifies a separate saline body south of the selected endpoint; none is assigned to the river.

scope_limits: No formal registry status is verified.
Neither absence of a printed channel in volcanic/sampling maps nor a regional endorheic classification proves the route is nonexistent or unnaturally connected.
The135.790km is the inventory display length, not a surveyed river length.
Precise banks, vertices, hydraulic operation and present wetness are outside this review.
Regional volcanic labels are not assigned to individual selected positions; a rough private orientation overlay is excluded from exact unit-association claims.

bounded_name_observations.name: La Salinilla / La Salina
bounded_name_observations.role: separately mapped southern saline body; not a verified receiving endpoint

records.region: La Purísima drainage, Sierra de la Giganta to the Pacific coast, Comondú and Loreto municipalities, Baja California Sur, Mexico.
records.geographic_disambiguation: La Purísima is directly attached to the joined middle/lower watercourse. The connected selected headward feeder can belong to this representative system without every reach bearing the same name. The hydrological study describes La Redonda and Comondú Viejo in its upper-course account, but those names are not assigned to every part of the chosen opening.
records.completion_scope: All 24 stored parts have ordinary source correspondence through the two complementary municipal originals. The chosen feeder, the municipal-boundary circuit, northern/westward joins, southward receiving valley, lower bends and actual coastal terminal are depicted. The 1996 state hydrological study corroborates the representative La Purísima identity. A single uniform hydronym is not imposed on every reach.
records.supported_name_scope: La Purísima is directly attached to the joined middle/lower watercourse. The connected selected headward feeder can belong to this representative system without every reach bearing the same name. The hydrological study describes La Redonda and Comondú Viejo in its upper-course account, but those names are not assigned to every part of the chosen opening.

scope_limits: The full chosen feeder has no securely read component hydronym. This does not prevent the connected selection from having a representative La Purísima system identity.
Exact boundaries between the study’s La Redonda, Comondú Viejo and La Purísima name scopes are not assigned to model vertices.
No formal name-registry verification, official river length, surveyed source/mouth, exact modern bank, continuous present flow or operational hydraulic assertion is made.

bounded_name_observations.name: La Redonda
bounded_name_observations.role: Name in the hydrological study’s upper principal-course narrative; not independently assigned to the entire chosen model opening.

bounded_name_observations.name: Comondú Viejo
bounded_name_observations.role: Upper-course name in the hydrological study and a watercourse entry in Loreto’s table; not a uniform name for every selected component.

bounded_name_observations.name: R. Cadegomo
bounded_name_observations.role: Municipal subbasin label; basin membership alone is not used to create a whole-river alias.

bounded_name_observations.name: Comondú
bounded_name_observations.role: Separate nearby southern drainage on the municipal and hydrological maps, distinct from the selected La Purísima corridor.

records.region: Coast Mountains, British Columbia, Canada: upper Elaho approach, Squamish valley and Howe Sound.
records.material_pending_reason: The actual selected glacial opening, continuous Elaho corridor and upper/middle Squamish through-links are not established by usable independently read cartography. Available prose supports component identity and tributary relationships, while lower-river map and orthophoto material supports the terminal corridor.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The receiving Squamish River system is supported, and Elaho River is the independently named headward component. Continuous geographic correspondence is incomplete for the selected opening and upper-to-middle route; this is not a completed whole-system naming finding.
records.completion_scope: All three selected fragments were considered. Inspected lower-river maps support the Cheakamus and Mamquam joining corridor and the actual Howe Sound terminal. The chosen glacial opening, continuous Elaho route, first fragment join and upper/middle Squamish links remain materially incomplete.
records.supported_name_scope: The receiving Squamish River system is supported, and Elaho River is the independently named headward component. Continuous geographic correspondence is incomplete for the selected opening and upper-to-middle route; this is not a completed whole-system naming finding.

scope_limits: Prose and names cannot substitute for the missing upper source-to-selected-route links. This is material-pending, not a completed unnamed-system scope hold.
Golder Figure1 credits MSRM watershed data. Its underlying drainage relationship to held DataBC/TRIM material was not affirmatively resolved; its map pixels were not read or used.
Chappaz2006 describes direct personal observations but does not georeference the selected opening or supply complete corridor cartography. His cited topographic maps were not acquired.
Historical mapping is used at ordinary corridor scale. Current glacier margins, berm configuration, bank positions and hydraulic operations are outside this assessment.
The representative system label does not mean every selected reach is called Squamish River. Elaho is a distinct named headward river.

bounded_name_observations.name: Elaho River
bounded_name_observations.role: Distinct glacial headward river entering Squamish River; assignment to every selected upper part remains provisional.

bounded_name_observations.name: Squamish River
bounded_name_observations.role: Receiving trunk and independently mapped lower river.

bounded_name_observations.name: Howe Sound
bounded_name_observations.role: Receiving sea inlet at the stored terminal; not a river name.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
